consensus_findings.description: Critical: `LocalEndpointService.sync_from_agents_config` does `getattr(agent, "model", None)`, but `AgentEntry` has no `model` field and the agents schema only added `endpoint_kind`/`base_url`. Endpoint-only agents therefore always catalog under `agent.name` (locked in by `test_agents_registry_local_endpoint_is_registered_for_probing`), so `POST /routing/select_model` can return a non-serving model id. Health probes hit `{base_url}/models` but never replace the catalog model from the probe payload, and review discovery resolves a different model via archetype/CLI/SDK fallbacks.

Critical: `RoutingService.select_model` always calls `choose(..., budget=ExplorationBudget())` with default `pct_used=0` / `usd_used=0` and persists `budget_state: {}`. The dual-ceiling gate in `exploration.py` therefore never exhausts, so exploration stays epsilon-open on every request instead of stopping after the configured task-share/USD ceilings. Decision provenance cannot show real budget burn-down.

Catalog filter strings interpolate raw values (task_type from the request's task_signals, vendor/model/endpoint_kind from refresher and probe rows) without percent-encoding. Both DatabaseClient backends split query_params on '&' (db.py:148 concatenates into the REST URL; db_postgres.py:280 parses parts), and the repo's convention is issue_service._encode_query_value for exactly this reason. An authenticated caller can POST task_signals.task_type='x&limit=0' or 'x&order=...' to alter the posterior query, and any OpenRouter model id containing '&' or '=' corrupts get_entry/upsert. Encode every filter value with the existing helper.

_candidate_payload hardcodes stale_catalog=False and CatalogService.list_candidates drops the row's derived staleness (computed by _with_derived_staleness) when building CandidateInput. The spec requires stale rows to be reported as stale and the Candidate contract carries stale_catalog for that purpose, yet every selection response and persisted decision claims a fresh catalog even when refresh has failed for days.

Only RoutingUnavailableError maps to 503. A DB outage in catalog.list_candidates or catalog.record_decision (httpx/asyncpg errors) surfaces as an unhandled 500, and record_decision runs after a valid selection so the caller gets a 500 for a decision that was computed but not persisted. The MCP tool select_model_for_task does not map RoutingUnavailableError at all, so the two transports disagree on the no-candidate failure mode. The synchronous seam only tolerates this because it catches everything, but external HTTP/MCP callers do not.

The spec says the refresher updates OpenRouter 'pricing and availability', but refresh() only upserts models present in the response. A model removed from OpenRouter keeps available=True forever and stays routable; its refreshed_at also never advances so it becomes 'stale' rather than unavailable, and stale rows are documented as still routable. Also item['id'] raises KeyError on a malformed entry, aborting mid-loop after partial upserts.

The scheduled 'ledger rollup' computes a full-month scan every 5 minutes and discards the dict; nothing is persisted, logged, or exposed, so the watchdog job is a pure read load with no observable effect. Separately, RoutingService.get_usage always returns by_model=[] and exploration_usd_used=0.0 because usage_summary never groups by model or sums rows with exploration=True, even though the ledger rows carry both fields. The UsageAggregate contract advertises both.

The adaptive branch maps the candidate's catalog vendor onto ResolvedArchetype.provider and drops endpoint_kind. For OpenRouter rows the refresher sets vendor to the model-id prefix (e.g. 'qwen' for 'qwen/qwen3-coder'), so a caller receives provider='qwen', model='qwen/qwen3-coder' with no indication it must dispatch via the OpenRouter endpoint. Existing provider semantics ('codex', 'claude', ...) select CLI/SDK adapters, so an adaptive selection is not actionable by current dispatchers. If adaptive dispatch is out of dg-00 scope, the wrapper should say so; if not, endpoint_kind needs to travel with the result.

OpenAPI declares task_signals.required=[archetype], but SelectModelRequest accepts any dict and _task_type silently routes an archetype-less request as 'unknown/medium-complexity'. Related contract drift in the same module: the 503 raised for no feasible candidate is not declared in v1.yaml; get_usage returns an undeclared top-level estimated_fraction and has no response_model; the 401 responses are declared as RFC 7807 problem documents but the coordinator's verify_api_key returns FastAPI's plain {'detail': ...} body.

Nit: `LedgerService.usage_summary` never builds `by_model` or `exploration_usd_used`, even though ledger rows already store vendor/model/endpoint_kind/exploration/actual_usd. `RoutingService.get_usage` therefore always returns `by_model: []` and `exploration_usd_used: 0.0` via `.get(..., default)`, despite OpenAPI `UsageAggregate` and the `/routing/usage` summary advertising per-model aggregates and exploration burn-down.

Nit: `select_model_endpoint` maps `RoutingUnavailableError` to HTTP 503, but `contracts/openapi/v1.yaml` only documents 200/401/422 for `POST /routing/select_model`. Clients generated from the contract will not handle the empty-candidate failure mode.

Nit: `CatalogService.upsert` updates an existing row with the full `CatalogEntry.to_row()` payload, and `DirectPostgresClient.update` writes Python `None` as SQL NULL. `OpenRouterRefresher` therefore nulls `p50_latency_ms`, `quota_headroom_pct`, `quota_reset_at`, and `quota_source` on every successful refresh and forces `available=True`, wiping non-pricing fields that refresh does not own.

The broad except in _probe wraps the success-path set_availability call, so a DB write failure after a healthy probe is reported as the endpoint being down (available=False). Conversely, if set_availability raises inside the except block, the exception escapes probe_all and aborts probing of the remaining endpoints, which the watchdog then records as a single job failure.

list_candidates issues one posteriors query per available catalog row on every select_model call (N+1), and OpenRouterRefresher.upsert does a get_entry plus insert/update per model, so a full refresh of OpenRouter's several hundred models costs 600+ sequential round trips. Both are on the hot or scheduled path and grow linearly with catalog size.

_adaptive_task_signals spreads the filtered signals and then unconditionally sets modality='programmatic', overriding any caller-supplied modality (the contract allows 'interactive'). Also, when ROUTING_ADAPTIVE is on but COORDINATION_API_URL is unset, every resolution spawns a thread and logs a warning, which is noisy at phase-resolution frequency; a one-time or rate-limited warning would suffice.

OpenRouter reports '-1' for dynamically priced models. _per_million converts that to a negative per-Mtok price, which would rank such models as cheaper than zero-cost local endpoints in the cost term.

_default_routing_jobs runs in WatchdogService.__init__ and parses the three interval env vars with int(); a malformed value raises ValueError and prevents the watchdog from constructing at all, taking the pre-existing stale-agent and vendor-health checks down with it. The same pattern exists in get_usage's float(ROUTING_MONTHLY_CEILING_USD), which turns a typo into a 500 on /routing/usage.

get_dispatch_configs now emits agents whose cli and sdk are both None. review_dispatcher.from_config_dict was updated, but any other consumer of /agents/dispatch-configs or this helper (vendor-status, quick-task, older skill copies) that assumes one block is present will hit AttributeError/KeyError or skip silently. This is a silent behavior change to an existing shared serializer.

test_catalog_read_uses_storage_only_and_derives_staleness asserts external_client.get was never awaited, but external_client is never given to CatalogService, so the 'no external call on the read path' assertion is vacuous and would pass even if list_entries called httpx directly. Likewise test_migrations_catalog only string-matches the SQL; idempotency (second apply preserves schema and data) is asserted by the spec but never executed.

Optional: `usage_summary` filters `routing_spend_ledger` with `occurred_at` range predicates, but migration `040_model_routing.sql` only indexes `date_trunc('month', occurred_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')` plus `endpoint_kind`. That expression index does not support the actual gte/lte access path used by usage/rollup.

none: The `ROUTING_ADAPTIVE` kill switch, bounded thread/queue timeout, and degrade-to-exact-static path in `resolve_archetype_for_phase` match the static-tier fallback requirement, and `test_delegation.py` pins flag-off equality, signal forwarding, error fallback, and timeout bounds.
